study_guide.title: Cane and the Rising Water

pages.text: Cane the Weather Dog had learned a lot about hurricanes. But there was one more thing to know — and it was the most important safety lesson of all.

"When people think of a hurricane, they think of wind and rain," said Cane. "But do you know what the biggest danger usually is? It's the water — and it comes in a special way. It's called storm surge." "Here's how it works," said Cane. He pushed a bowl of water with his paw, and the water sloshed up and over the edge. "When a hurricane blows toward the shore, its strong wind pushes the ocean water up onto the land — higher than normal. That rising water is the storm surge." "The surge can come up fast," said Cane, "and cover streets and yards that are usually dry. That's called a flood. Because the water is so powerful, storm surge is the part of a hurricane we have to be the most careful about."
pages.ask: Have you ever heard those two words — storm surge? Can you gently push some bath water and watch it pile up on one side?

pages.text: "So here's the smart, safe thing we do," Cane said. "When grown-ups say to move away from the water, we go — to higher ground. Higher ground is land that's up higher, where the surge can't reach." "Weather people even have a saying," said Cane. "Run from the water. Hide from the wind. It means: get away from storm surge, and stay safe inside from the wind."
pages.ask: Point to something up high in your room. That's like higher ground — up and away from the water!

pages.text: A big storm was coming. The grown-ups said it was time to move away from the water and go to a safer place on higher ground. Cane's family didn't panic — they had a plan, so they calmly packed up and went early. "See?" said Cane, safe on high, dry ground. "The water is the biggest danger — so we move away from it, calm and early. That's how we stay safe. Great job, weather watcher!"

study_guide.rule: Storm surge is ocean water pushed onto land — so we move away from the water to higher ground!
